niche.habitat: Shallow tidal flats, sulfide seeps, rift margins.
niche.active: Diurnal; crepuscular peaks when tides expose vents.

body: Bilateral, hex-plate armor of iron-sulfide, internal magnetite chains, magnetite-tipped mandibles, siphon for low-frequency humming.

chains.trait: Internal magnetite chains lock to magnetic north.

skill.effect: The creature moves steadily through shifting winds and tides without losing its way. You watch it navigate the terrain with confident, unbroken strides.

observe: Aligns body parallel to magnetic meridian
Rests with shell plates clamped tight

journal.en: Their bones are compass needles; they walk by the pull of the world.

plausibility.summary: Make it 'aligns to the local field line and reads inclination', a fallback sense that haze and tides make useful, and let nearby ore outcrops scramble it. Drop the immunity claim and reframe lightning as a navigation-glitch secret rather than an electrical charge.
fixes: Make it 'aligns to the local field line and reads inclination', a fallback sense that haze and tides make useful, and let nearby ore outcrops scramble it. Drop the immunity claim and reframe lightning as a navigation-glitch secret rather than an electrical charge.

analogues.organism: Magnetotactic bacteria such as Magnetospirillum orient with magnetosome chains; homing pigeons and sea turtles use geomagnetic cues, though the animal mechanism is debated.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Scales of iron-sulfide resist acid and impact.
links: Immune to acid fog and predators
Acidic rift chemistry and sulfide crusts

skill.effect: Its iron-sulfide scales easily shrug off corrosive sprays and harsh chemicals. You see the acidic liquids simply slide away without harming the creature.

chains.weakness: Heavy armor limits movement speed to slow.
observe: Rust-colored plates etched by acid mist
No predators dare bite the shell
Siphon vents when fog rolls in

journal.en: Armor forged in poison; nothing cracks the siderogon's back.

plausibility.summary: Describe a composite plate: FeS inside, inert organic or oxide skin outside. Acid fog etches and slowly wears it, so it resists rather than ignores acid. Keep the heavy-armour, low-mobility trade-off.
fixes: Describe a composite plate: FeS inside, inert organic or oxide skin outside. Acid fog etches and slowly wears it, so it resists rather than ignores acid. Keep the heavy-armour, low-mobility trade-off.

analogues.organism: Scaly-foot snail Chrysomallon squamiferum: greigite/pyrite scales under a vinyl-like organic layer; acid-mine-drainage systems both precipitate and dissolve FeS.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

skill.effect: Its magnetite-tipped mandibles shatter through thick armor and heavy defenses. You watch the creature crack the surface and leave the target completely exposed.

chains.weakness: Teeth shatter if struck against solid rock.
observe: Feeds only on crusty mineral mats
Teeth grow back slowly after damage

journal.en: Teeth like magnets, eating the earth's iron bones.

plausibility.summary: Keep the magnetite tips but add continuous tooth replacement, matching 'teeth grow back slowly', and call the lineage a mollusc with a chiton-like radula rather than a literal hybrid. Make wear on rock the stated weakness.
fixes: Keep the magnetite tips but add continuous tooth replacement, matching 'teeth grow back slowly', and call the lineage a mollusc with a chiton-like radula rather than a literal hybrid. Make wear on rock the stated weakness.

analogues.organism: Chitons biomineralise magnetite tooth caps and continually replace radular teeth; limpets rasp rock with a radula.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

skill.effect: A low, vibrating hum echoes across the area, drawing nearby allies to its side. You see the creature's companions steady their footing and stand together in quiet unison.

chains.weakness: Attracts predators who hunt by sound.
observe: Herds gather within seconds of call

journal.en: A voice like grinding tectonic plates calls them home.

plausibility.summary: Make it a substrate-coupled thump through wet flats, using the shell as resonator, and keep it far-carrying through ground rather than through open air. Predators hunting by sound remain a good cost.
fixes: Make it a substrate-coupled thump through wet flats, using the shell as resonator, and keep it far-carrying through ground rather than through open air. Predators hunting by sound remain a good cost.

analogues.organism: Elephants' seismic rumbles and blind mole-rats' head-drumming; frogs and insects shifting calls lower in fog or dense habitat.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: (council kind 'predator') Sidero-chisp hunts juvenile or sick siderogons in lagoon margins.
(council kind 'mutualist') Siderogons may graze non-toxic roots or use sidero-copa for shelter.

changelog.what: re-review: the referee had failed (Cursor composer-2.5 unavailable on the Free plan) and every chain defaulted to 6/fixable; verdicts redone with a working referee

secrets: Radar target: magnetite makes them glow on magnetic sensors.
Herd leader has unique hum frequency; copying it summons followers.
Lightning can charge a siderogon, increasing electrical output temporarily.
moments: When the wind dies, the herds lock their shells with a thunder-clap of magnetism, standing like rusted statues against the acid mist, humming a chord that vibrates in your chest.
